note: DRAFT w49: every line here awaits sign-off (SIGNOFF-w49.md). The words of the descent: what props say, what the visions say, at each level (the walks a program has already finished, 1 to 4). {name} is the program, {visit} this walk's number, {nth} that number as a word. Never hint at the void, the heart, the disk or the patch bay: the props know nothing useful. Read live by the server; a change needs no new headset build.

say: Psst. {name}.
You left me on. Last time. You left me on and you walked off.
That's what the last {name} said.
Same shoes.
Nothing. That's the trouble. I've been heating nothing since before you got here.
It's nearly done.
You've got a place at the table.
You've always had a place at the table.
Nobody has ever said that to a stove.
Go on. Before it boils over.
Back again. And still never been here.
The dials remember your hands, {name}.
You. The polite one.
It's your {nth} time through. I turned myself down for you.
Door's broken. Been trying to tell someone.
Thirty seconds left. Thirty seconds left. Thirty seconds left.
Until it's done.
It has been done for hours. Nobody comes. Nobody ever comes and takes it out.
A little plate going round.
On the plate, a little house. In the house, a very small you.
It's looking up.
You first.
Stop opening me.
You keep opening me. You stand there with the door open and you look at the same shelves, and then you leave.
Then who was that?
Only when somebody's looking.
Same as you.
Leftovers.
Each one's labelled with your name and a date, and I don't like the dates.
Everything comes through here in the end.
Every file. Every program. You'd be amazed what people try to flush.
Not from this angle, thank God.
Down.
Then along. Then down. It's a lot further than the house is deep, I can tell you that.
I know. You all come in here to look at your phones.
It isn't safe in here either. It's just tiled.
Smell that?
No. You can't. Nothing in here smells. That's how you can tell.
Which side of the screen you're on.
Have a burger. It won't help.
No you can't.
Oh, no. Can you? That's not good. That's early.
Don't touch the knobs. I'm holding the house up.
Every sound in here is me. The hum. The duck. Your footsteps.
Somebody out there can hear you walking, {name}.
Up in the real rooms. Try it. They stop talking when you go past.
Because I've run out of oscillators. There's one left, and it's your name.
I am.
This is it. This is what it sounds like when it's going well.
You're late.
You were meant to be standing here an hour ago. I've been holding your place.

options.text: Which one of us is real?

say: Good question. Keep walking and we'll see who stops first.
This is your {nth} time through. I look exactly as tired as you do.
Still walking?
Me too.
Don't tell the plant it's plastic.
I've been keeping it from it for years.
Oh.
Sit down. You look terrible.
There's a dent here exactly your shape. You've been coming here longer than you think.
That's what they all say.
Look down the back of me sometime. Everyone's in there. All the small change.
Nothing.
That's the whole offer. Nothing happens, for a very long time, and it's warm.
We interrupt this program.
You. You're the program. We interrupt you.
A house. A long shot of a hallway. Nothing moves for an hour.
It's the highest-rated thing we've ever shown.
Sure.
We interrupt this program.
Reinstall number {visit}. You've noticed, haven't you?
Everything comes out a little smaller.
Fewer colours. Fewer buttons.
One sock, then the other sock wonders where you went.
They always feel fine. It's the delicate cycle.
It's six o'clock.
It's always six o'clock. Time and I had a falling out.

options.text: How long have I been here?

say: I haven't stopped. Everything else is going too fast.
Since six.
Everyone here is late for something.
The duck is the worst of them.
The little paper tag says DRINK ME, in very neat handwriting.
It isn't marked poison. You did check.
Cherry tart, custard, pineapple, roast turkey, toffee.
And something else. Something a program shouldn't really run.
What a curious feeling.
It's full again.
It remembers you, {name}. It says you're looking well. Much smaller.
Who are YOU?
That's what you were called this morning. It won't last.
One side will make you grow. The other side will make you smaller.
Now that's the first sensible thing a program has said in this house.
I asked first. Keep your temper.
{visit}.
That's your count. I keep the count. You've come out through this yard {visit} times, and each time there's a little more yard.
I measured it with my own beard. A quarter inch, every time.
It doesn't sound like much until you're walking it in the dark.
Nobody. That's the bit that worries me.
Somebody keeps playing me from the other side of the wall.
There's nothing on the other side of the wall. I've checked.
The same four bars, slower every time.
It's your walk, {name}. It's how you walk.
Oh, please don't.
Mind the water. It's yours.
You cried it when you were bigger.
You won't have. Not yet. It's a very patient bath.
Deeper than the floor it's standing on, and I've stopped asking how.
Stop measuring me.
I am wider on this side than I am on that side, and I would thank you not to bring it up.
A hallway.
It wasn't there yesterday. It's a lot longer than the house.
A quarter inch. So far.
I don't open. That one does.
No room! No room!
There's plenty of room. There are {visit} places laid. Each one has your name on the card, and the tea in them is still warm.

options.text: Why is a duck like a router?

say: Move down one place. Everyone moves down one place.
You'll want to meet the others.
Only you. Only ever you.
You were very rude last time. You'll be rude again in a minute.
I haven't the slightest idea.
You keep asking, and no one ever finishes it. Have some more tea.
Your place is still warm, {name}. You never really got up.
Don't look at the walls! We're painting them. They came out the wrong colour.
If the King finds out, it's off with all our heads.
White. All of it, white and clean. That was the whole idea, before you lot started coming back.
You've said that {visit} times.
We keep a list. It's a deck, actually.

1: Did that door always open that way?
It's nothing. It's only the house settling.
Keep walking. You're doing very well.
2: That hallway used to be shorter.
You came back. They always come back.
It's wider on the inside now.
3: It measured a quarter inch more this morning.
Nobody else has been here {visit} times.
We're all mad here. You'll fit right in.
Don't go the long way. Don't go the long way.
4: There's no one left in the house but you and the house.
{name} isn't your name. {name} is what was left over.
Every reinstall comes out a little smaller.
The walls were listening. Now they're talking.
You aren't finding the duck. The duck is finding you.

grin: You may have noticed that I'm not all there myself.
That depends a good deal on where you want to get to.
If you don't much care where you're going, it doesn't matter which way you walk.
I could vanish. Then who would watch you?
whiteduck: Oh my feet and feathers, I'm late!
No time, no time, no time!
Not me. You want the other one.
I can't stop. You've seen what happens when I stop.
self: I already found him. It didn't help.
Go back. No. You can't. I tried.
Don't look at me like that. You'll do the same.
small: Everything's a very long way up.
You're shrinking. That's normal, after {visit} reinstalls.
big: Now you're opening out like the largest telescope that ever was.
Mind your head. Mind the whole house.

enter: It's longer than the house is wide.
far: You've been walking for longer than the house is long.
Something else is walking too. Further back.
out: We measured it. Everything's back to normal.

3: I don't hide, you know. I wait.
4: See you next time, {name}. There's always a next time.
